toc.label: The Real Cost of Missed Calls

sections.heading: The Real Cost of a Missed Call
sections.body:
For a local HVAC company, a single new customer is worth $300–$1,200 in first-year revenue. If your phone rings 20 times a day and you miss 6 of those calls, and even 2 of those 6 would have booked — that's $600–$2,400 per day in lost potential revenue.

Most service businesses don't track missed calls because they're not visible. You only see what came in. You never see what walked away.

sections.heading: Run the Math on Your Business
sections.body:
Here's a conservative calculation for a local plumbing company:

- **Daily inbound calls:** 15
- **Miss rate during busy hours:** 30% = 4–5 missed calls/day
- **Conversion rate if called back within 5 minutes:** ~40%
- **Average job value:** $350
- **Missed revenue per day:** 2 jobs × $350 = $700
- **Missed revenue per month:** ~$14,000

Now ask yourself: if you could recover even 1 extra job per day by sending an instant text when you miss a call, what would that be worth in a year?
sections.callout: A plumber missing 2 jobs per day at $350 each = $8,400/month in unrecovered revenue.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Miss a Call Without a System
sections.body:
Without automation, here's what happens:

1. Your phone rings. You're on a job, driving, or with a client.
2. The call goes to voicemail.
3. The caller hangs up — 62% don't leave a voicemail (BrightLocal, 2024).
4. They open Google and call the next business.
5. You call back 2 hours later. They've already booked someone else.

With missed-call text-back, what happens instead:

1. Your phone rings. You miss it.
2. **Within 30 seconds**, the caller receives a text: *"Hey, this is [Business Name] — sorry we missed you! What can we help you with today?"*
3. They reply. You're now in a conversation while they're still deciding.
4. You book the job from your phone before you're even back to your truck.

sections.heading: Why Your Follow-Up Isn't Working
sections.body:
The #1 reason leads don't convert isn't price, fit, or timing — it's that nobody followed up consistently.

Here's what typically happens:
- Day 1: You send an intro email.
- Day 3: No reply. You feel awkward. You move on.
- Day 30: That lead signs with a competitor who followed up 7 times.

**The data is brutal:** 80% of non-routine sales happen after at least 5 contacts, but 44% of salespeople give up after just one follow-up (Marketing Donut / Invesp). The gap between those two numbers is where your revenue is disappearing.

The problem isn't your product. It's that following up 5+ times manually feels pushy, gets forgotten, and doesn't scale.

sections.heading: The 7-Touch Follow-Up System That Doesn't Feel Spammy
sections.body:
The goal isn't volume — it's sequenced multi-channel contact that adds value at each touchpoint. Here's the cadence we use:

- **Day 1:** Intro email
- **Day 2:** SMS check-in
- **Day 4:** Value email (case study, tip, or relevant resource)
- **Day 6:** Voicemail drop
- **Day 8:** Final value SMS
- **Day 10:** "Last touch" email with a clear soft close
- **Day 14:** Breakup email — creates urgency and often generates a reply

This sequence spans two weeks, touches all three channels (email, SMS, phone), and gives every lead a fair chance to convert.

steps.body: Hey [First Name], I've reached out a few times and want to be respectful of your time. If now isn't the right moment, completely understood — just let me know and I'll follow up in a few months. If you are still interested, here's a link to grab 15 minutes: [Calendar Link]

sections.heading: What Local SEO Is — and Why Georgetown Businesses Can Win It
sections.body:
When someone types "HVAC Georgetown MA" or "best salon near me" into Google, three businesses appear at the top in the Map Pack. The businesses below them are essentially invisible — 70% of users click one of those three results and never scroll further (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey, 2024).

Local SEO is the process of getting your business into those top three spots. It's not the same as regular SEO — it's specifically about signals that tell Google your business is real, active, local, and trusted by actual customers.

The good news: most Georgetown and North Shore businesses are not optimizing for this at all. The barrier to ranking is lower than you think if you're consistent.

sections.heading: Step 1: Optimize Your Google Business Profile
sections.body:
Your Google Business Profile (GBP) is the single highest-leverage thing you can do for local SEO. It's what drives your appearance in the Map Pack.

**The basics that most businesses skip:**
- **Business category:** Choose the most specific primary category possible. "Plumber" outperforms "Home Services" every time.
- **Business hours:** Keep them accurate and updated. Google factors responsiveness.
- **Photos:** Profiles with 100+ photos get significantly more calls than those with under 10. Add photos of your team, your work, your location, and your vehicles.
- **Services section:** List every service you offer with keyword-rich descriptions. "Emergency drain cleaning in Georgetown MA" beats "Drain services."
- **Posts:** Google rewards active profiles. Post weekly — a special offer, a completed project, a tip for homeowners.
- **Q&A:** Seed your own Q&A section with common questions your customers ask.

**Georgetown-specific tip:** In your GBP description, mention Georgetown, Rowley, Boxford, Groveland, and the surrounding towns you serve. Google uses this to understand your service radius.

sections.heading: Step 2: Fix Your NAP Consistency
sections.body:
NAP stands for Name, Address, Phone. Google cross-references your business information across the entire web. If your name is "Georgetown Electric" on Google but "Georgetown Electric Co." on Yelp and "Georgetown Electrical Services" on your website — Google loses confidence in your listing and drops your rank.

**Where to check and fix your NAP:**
- Google Business Profile
- Your website header and contact page
- Yelp
- Apple Maps / Bing Places
- Facebook Business Page
- Better Business Bureau
- Yellow Pages
- Chamber of Commerce listing

**Use the exact same format everywhere.** If you abbreviate "Street" as "St." on Google, abbreviate it everywhere. If your phone number is (978) 555-1234, don't list it as 978-555-1234 on other directories. The consistency is what matters.

This takes about 2 hours to audit and fix once. Most businesses never do it.

sections.heading: Step 3: Build Review Velocity (Not Just Review Count)
sections.body:
Google doesn't just look at how many reviews you have — it looks at how frequently you're getting new ones. A business with 40 reviews all received in 2022 ranks lower than a business with 35 reviews that gets 3–5 new reviews per month.

**How to build review velocity:**
1. Ask every customer for a review — in person, immediately after the job
2. Send an automated review request via SMS 24 hours after job completion
3. Include a direct Google review link (not your homepage)
4. Respond to every review — positive and negative — within 48 hours

**Georgetown example:** A Georgetown landscaping company went from 12 Google reviews to 67 in 4 months by adding an automated post-job SMS that sent a review link directly to the customer's phone. Their Map Pack ranking moved from position 6 to position 2 for "landscaper Georgetown MA" over the same period.

CasperPortal automates this entire process — review requests fire automatically after a job is marked complete.

sections.heading: Step 4: Build Local Citations
sections.body:
A citation is any mention of your business name, address, and phone number on another website. The more quality citations you have (especially on authoritative directories), the more Google trusts your business is real and local.

**Priority citation sources for North Shore businesses:**
- Yelp
- Apple Maps
- Bing Places
- Yellow Pages
- Angi (formerly Angie's List)
- HomeAdvisor
- Better Business Bureau (BBB)
- Essex County Chamber of Commerce
- Massachusetts Business listings
- Local newspaper directories (The Daily News, Haverhill Gazette)

Aim for 20–40 consistent citations as a foundation. Don't pay for spammy citation blasts — quality and consistency matter more than volume.

sections.heading: Step 5: Target Local Keywords on Your Website
sections.body:
Your GBP alone isn't enough. Your website needs to reinforce your location signals.

**Local keyword patterns to target:**
- "[Service] Georgetown MA" (e.g., "plumber Georgetown MA")
- "[Service] near me" (Google fills in the location)
- "[Service] Essex County"
- "[Service] North Shore MA"

**Where to use them:**
- Your homepage H1 and meta title
- Your service pages (one page per core service)
- Your footer (include your full address and NAP)
- Your blog (write locally-specific content)

**Example:** Instead of a generic "Services" page, create a page titled "Plumbing Services in Georgetown, MA — Emergency & Scheduled Repairs" with a unique 500-word description of what you do in Georgetown specifically.

If you serve multiple towns — Georgetown, Rowley, Ipswich, Newburyport — create individual location pages for each. Don't use the same content on every page. Google penalizes duplicate location pages.
sections.callout: Local SEO is not a one-time project. It's a monthly discipline. The businesses that win locally are the ones that show up consistently.

sections.heading: The Single-Channel Trap Killing Local Businesses
sections.body:
Most North Shore small businesses rely on one primary lead source:
- **Referrals** — great when business is good, terrifying when it dries up
- **Google Ads** — works until your budget runs out or a competitor outbids you
- **Facebook** — algorithm changes tank your reach overnight
- **Word of mouth** — impossible to predict or scale

When you rely on one channel and that channel stalls, your entire pipeline stalls. The businesses that survive and grow on the North Shore have one thing in common: they have multiple ways to generate and nurture leads simultaneously.

You don't need 10 channels. You need 3 that work together.

sections.heading: Channel 1 — Google Business Profile (Free, High-Intent Traffic)
sections.body:
Your Google Business Profile is the highest-leverage free marketing tool available to any local business. When someone searches "contractor Newburyport MA" or "salon near me," Google shows the top 3 local results in the Map Pack before any paid ads or organic results.

**What to do every week:**
- Post a photo of recent work (before/after, team on-site, completed project)
- Respond to any new reviews within 24 hours
- Add any new services or seasonal offers to your listing
- Monitor your "Questions & Answers" section and respond

**Priority:** This channel brings **high-intent buyers** — people actively looking for your service right now. It should be the first channel you optimize, not an afterthought.

**Budget required:** $0. Time required: 30 minutes/week.

sections.heading: Channel 2 — SMS Follow-Up (The Fastest ROI Channel)
sections.body:
SMS has a 98% open rate versus 20% for email (SimpleTexting, 2024). For local service businesses, it's the fastest way to re-engage a lead who went cold, remind a customer about an appointment, or recover someone who didn't book.

**The 3 SMS automations every local business needs:**
1. **Missed-call text-back** — instant SMS when a call goes unanswered
2. **Appointment reminder** — automated text 24 hours and 2 hours before appointments
3. **Win-back campaign** — SMS to customers who haven't booked in 90+ days

**Example message (win-back):**
*"Hey [First Name], it's been a while! We're running a [seasonal offer] this month — want to get back on the schedule? Reply here or book at [link]."*

**A Haverhill auto detailing shop** ran a win-back SMS to 180 past customers and booked 22 appointments in 5 days. At $150 average ticket, that's $3,300 in revenue from one text message.

**Budget required:** Included in CasperPortal. Time to set up: 45 minutes.
sections.callout: SMS win-backs are the fastest way to generate revenue from customers you already have.

sections.heading: Channel 3 — Email Nurture (The Long-Game Channel)
sections.body:
Email is not dead for local businesses — it's underused. Most local businesses either don't email their list at all, or they blast promotions with no strategy.

The right email nurture system does two things:
1. **Stays top-of-mind** for people who aren't ready to buy yet
2. **Converts warm leads** who need a few more touchpoints before booking

**A simple local business email calendar:**
- **Monthly:** "What's new at [Business Name]" — updates, seasonal services, new team members
- **Quarterly:** A helpful tip or guide related to your service
- **As-needed:** Time-sensitive offer with a clear deadline

**What to avoid:** Blasting "20% off this weekend!" with no context. Give people a reason to stay subscribed — tips, education, local community involvement.

**Budget required:** Included in CasperPortal. Time to build: 2 hours upfront, 30 minutes/month to maintain.

sections.heading: How the 3 Channels Create a Lead Machine
sections.body:
Each channel covers a different stage of the customer journey:

- **Google Business Profile** brings in new, high-intent customers who are searching right now
- **SMS** converts and re-engages leads quickly, with high open rates
- **Email** nurtures the people who aren't ready yet and keeps past customers coming back

**The loop looks like this:**
1. New customer finds you on Google
2. They call or fill out a form
3. If they don't book immediately → SMS follow-up sequence starts
4. They book and complete a service
5. They receive an automated review request (SMS)
6. They join your email list
7. Monthly email keeps them connected
8. In 90 days, win-back SMS goes out

This loop runs without you. Each channel feeds the next.

sections.heading: What AI Client Support Actually Means for a Small Business
sections.body:
When most people hear "AI client support," they think of a giant chatbot that frustrates customers. That's the wrong frame.

For a small business, AI automation in client support means:
- A text message goes out automatically when a call is missed
- A new inquiry gets an instant reply at 11pm — not a response the next morning
- A client asking "what time is my appointment?" gets an answer in seconds without you touching your phone
- A client who hasn't heard from you in 30 days gets a check-in message automatically

None of this requires AI in the science-fiction sense. It requires well-built automation — triggered messages, smart routing, and rules-based responses. CasperPortal calls this AI-assisted workflows, and for most small businesses, it's the single highest-leverage technology they can implement.

sections.heading: What Should Be Automated (The Right Candidates)
sections.body: These are the support tasks that are high-volume, low-complexity, and time-sensitive — perfect for automation:
steps: Missed-call text-back — instant SMS when you don't answer
New inquiry auto-reply — acknowledges the message immediately and sets expectations for response time
Appointment confirmation and reminders — 24 hours and 2 hours before
FAQ responses — hours, location, pricing range, service availability
Post-service follow-up — thank-you message + review request
Reschedule trigger — automated message when an appointment is missed or cancelled
30/60/90-day re-engagement — automatic check-in for past clients
sections.body2: These are tasks you're currently doing manually that take 5–20 minutes each. If you handle 10–15 client interactions per day, you're spending 50–150 minutes daily on work that could run automatically.
sections.callout: 10 client interactions per day × 10 minutes each = 100 minutes. Automation reclaims 80+ minutes of that.

sections.heading: What Should NOT Be Automated
sections.body:
Automation fails when it tries to replace human judgment in complex situations. Do not automate:

- **Complaint handling** — an upset customer needs a real human response, not a template
- **Price negotiations** — context matters; let your team handle these personally
- **Complex scheduling with special requirements** — automation works for standard bookings, not custom arrangements
- **Emotional situations** — a client calling about a medical concern, a legal matter, or a stressful personal situation needs a human voice

**The rule:** If the interaction requires empathy, judgment, or context that a template can't capture — it should escalate to a human. CasperPortal workflows are built with this in mind: when a contact uses specific trigger words (complaint, urgent, cancel, refund), the automation stops and notifies your team directly.

sections.heading: Automation vs. Hiring Part-Time Support: The Real Comparison
sections.body:
Many business owners think about hiring part-time front desk or support staff to handle client communication. Here's what that actually costs:

- Part-time support (15 hrs/week) in Massachusetts: $18–$22/hour
- Weekly cost: $270–$330
- Monthly cost: $1,080–$1,320
- Plus: training time, turnover risk, benefits consideration, scheduling complexity

For comparison, CasperPortal's full platform — including AI-assisted automation for all the workflows listed above — is $297/month.

**That's $783–$1,023 less per month than a part-time hire**, and the automation works 24/7, never calls in sick, and doesn't need two weeks of onboarding.

To be clear: automation doesn't replace great staff for complex tasks. It replaces the repetitive, time-consuming work that doesn't require a human, freeing your team for higher-value interactions.

sections.heading: Your Reviews Are Selling for You (Or Against You)
sections.body:
98% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses (BrightLocal, 2024). In a town like Georgetown or Haverhill, your reputation isn't just word-of-mouth anymore — it's digital.

When someone searches for your service, they make a split-second decision based on two numbers: your star rating and your review count. If you have a 4.8 with 12 reviews and your competitor has a 4.6 with 150 reviews, they win. Every time.

sections.heading: Google Cares About 'Freshness' (Review Velocity)
sections.body:
Most business owners think they just need "a lot" of reviews. Google's algorithm is smarter. It looks at **Review Velocity** — how many new reviews you're getting consistently.

10 reviews in the last month is worth more for your ranking than 100 reviews from three years ago. This is why you need a system that asks for reviews every single week, not a one-time "push" where you email your whole list once a year.

sections.heading: The Automated Ask: SMS vs. Email
sections.body:
If you email a review link, it has a 20% open rate and a 2% click rate. If you text a review link, it has a 98% open rate and a 15-20% click rate.

**The CasperPortal Workflow:**
1. Job is marked 'Complete' in your pipeline
2. Wait 2 hours (while the customer is still happy with the result)
3. Send SMS: *"Hey [First Name], thanks for choosing us! Would you mind leaving us a quick review? It helps us out a ton: [Link]"*
4. If no review after 3 days → Send one gentle reminder SMS.

This system alone typically increases review volume by 300-500% within the first 90 days.

sections.heading: The 'Feedback Loop': Stopping Negative Reviews Before They Happen
sections.body:
One of the biggest fears of asking for reviews is getting a 1-star rating in public. Smart reputation management uses a "feedback loop."

Instead of sending every customer straight to Google, you can ask for a rating first (1-5 stars). If they pick 4 or 5, send them to Google. If they pick 1, 2, or 3, send them to a private feedback form so you can fix the issue before it becomes a public stain on your reputation.

sections.heading: Responding to Reviews: The SEO Multiplier
sections.body:
Google explicitly states that responding to reviews improves your local SEO. It shows you're an active, engaged business. But more importantly, it shows *future* customers that you care.

**Pro Tip:** When you respond, use your local keywords. *"Thanks for the review, Sarah! We love being the top-rated plumber in Georgetown MA."* This helps Google connect your business to those specific search terms.
sections.callout: A business that responds to 100% of reviews ranks significantly higher than one that ignores them.
